html:
The cashew tree, native to Brazil, was brought to Mozambique by the Portuguese in the 16th century, and by the early 1970s Mozambique was the largest producer of cashew nuts in the world.

The trees spread along the coastal plains, where peasants gathered the nuts and sold them, and processing factories employed thousands, many of them women. Cashew was one of the colony's main exports, a crop also central to Guinea-Bissau on the other side of Africa.

Production collapsed in the civil war, and in the 1990s, under pressure from the World Bank, the government allowed raw nuts to be exported, closing most factories. The crop has since recovered, but India and Vietnam now lead the trade. It remains vital in northern Mozambique.
sum: The cashew tree, native to Brazil, was brought to Mozambique by the Portuguese in the 16th century, and by the early 1970s Mozambique was the largest producer of cashew nuts in the world.
